narrative.title: Demolition-Permit Walkthrough
narrative.scenario: A demolition contractor surveys a building shaped like a binary tree of structural bays. Safety law forbids logging a bay for teardown until every bay beneath it — the whole left wing and then the whole right wing — has already been inspected. Only after both wings are cleared does the crew sign off the bay itself. The signed-off sequence is what the permit office receives.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array of node values in postorder: visit the left subtree, then the right subtree, then the node.

testCases.explanation: Left subtree finishes as 4,5,2; right subtree as 6,3; the root lands last.
A single node has no children, so it is visited first and last.

hintLevels: Level 1: Postorder defers the parent until both of its subtrees are fully handled — children always win.
Level 2: Move the recording beat to the end of the recursion: recurse left, recurse right, record node.
Level 3: The root of any subtree appears last in its own postorder slice — that anchor helps reconstruct or validate trees.
